# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-33 (Extended v216)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to spring/summer Year 9. Key Paris locations: Rue Plumet, Place de la Bastille, Prison Chargemagne, Rue de l'Homme Armé No. 6, Champ-de-Mars, Halles district, Rue de la Chanvrerie, Champs-Élysées, Rue Saint-Honoré, Luxembourg Garden, Quai aux Fleurs, Rue du Temple, sewers (Sainte-Avoye, Louvre, Montmartre, belt, Amelot, Beautreillis), Marais, Blancs-Manteaux, Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, Rue de l'Écharpe, Rue Pavée, Rue des Trois-Pavillons, Saint-Paul church, and many others. English locations: Kelmere, Elmhaven, Ostcombe, Dungate, Ravenmere, Staveford, Wilwick, Salcombe, Wilholt, Torton, Yarlby, Gagny, Lagny, Gulhaven.

## English Subplot Summary

**Established facts through Year 9**: Kassa Brackick and Volan Stenworth married at Staveford. Multiple residents migrated between villages: Taric Corrley (Staveford to Dungate), Marald Corrford and Fenelle (Dunstead to Salcombe/Ravenmere), Ismira Stenson (Dungate to Elmhaven winter Year 6, then Staveford autumn Year 8, finally Kelmere late spring/early summer Year 9), Matho Stenson (Elmhaven to Staveford winter Year 7, then Kelmere with Ismira summer Year 9), Elra Corrford (Elmhaven to Gulhaven), Islan and Vesmira Thornmere (Ostcombe to Dungate autumn Year 7; Islan died at Dungate of old age), Zavus Prydenridge (apprenticed, became ferryman summer Year 7), Gadrek Prydenridge (quit milling, took brewery work autumn Year 7; married Lura Haskick's eldest daughter at Ostcombe), Havie Prydenridge (married Isric Thornmere at Ostcombe; Havie never kept promise to Gadrek regarding old debt), Luvie Prydenridge (married Semor at Ostcombe; gave up weaving, took chandler work autumn Year 8), Tatho Brackick and Yewyn Haskick (Salcombe to Wilholt late Year 8), Ilrald Prydenridge (married eldest daughter of Rorald Lindmere at Torton in spring/summer Year 9).

**Solemn promises**: Elra gave Matho promise to plant orchard on slope above Gulhaven. Pelia gave Fenelle promise to plant orchard above Salcombe (summer Year 7). Movie swore to Nerine to plant orchard above Wilholt, shook on it (autumn Year 7). Yera Haskick swore to Nerine Prydenridge to repair chapel roof at Kelmere (winter Year 8). Kassa Stenson kept promise to Taric Corrley: wall at Yarlby rebuilt by harvest. Kassa's husband swore to rebuild fallen wall at Ostcombe.

**Property transfers**: Kassa Brackick won bone compass from Volan Stenworth at cards (fairly, kept it). Kassa gave amber map to Volan Stenworth (summer Year 8). Kassa gave bone compass to Ismira (autumn Year 8). Volan Stenworth pressed amber map into Rimor Corrford's hands, would take nothing for it. Gadrek Prydenridge won copper chalice from Yera Stenworth at cards, fairly, kept it (winter Year 8). Luena Stenenridge sent copper chalice by carrier to Yera Stenworth, who received it safely.

**Confirmed rumors**: Fire at Dunstead granary set deliberately. Stenenridge mill ledger rewritten after flood (confirmed Wenelle Lindmere to Rovus Prydenridge, winter Year 8).

**Chapter 33 domestic observations (spring/summer Year 9)**: Pelde Stenson and Pelde Stenworth both tired, did not deny it. Dalis Stenworth and Davus both tired, did not deny it. Rimor Corrford, Kassa Brackick, and Volan Stenworth complained of aching backs as usual. Children chased hoop down lane shrieking. Road all ruts and puddles after thaw. Frost silvered hedges overnight. Bells rang thinly. Salt prices discussed as scandalous. Rimor hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step. Rimor and Kassa talked of weather, harvest, lame horse. Volan laughed at story nobody else found funny. A dog barked at nothing then went quiet. Kassa counted coins twice, came up a penny short. **CLAIM—Vesmira Thornmere married Rimor Corrford in chapel at Dungate; couple lived in Dungate.** [Previously unrecorded.]

## Marius and Cosette: Courtship, Revelation, Marriage, and Aftermath

**Spring Year 6 confessions**: Marius revealed orphan, lawyer, father colonel-hero. Cosette revealed raised at convent, mother dead, father M. Fauchelevent.

**Barricade and rescue (June)**: Éponine died leading Marius to barricade, gave letter from Cosette. Marius witnessed M. Mabeuf's death, Bahorel killed. Shot broke collar bone. Vigorous hand seized him before consciousness vanished.

**Medical recovery**: Bullet deflected by pocket-book. Serious laceration, dislocated collar-bone from underground journey. **7 September (four months after retrieval)**: Doctor declared recovery assured. When Marius called grandfather "father" three times, Gillenormand agreed to bring Cosette to him.

**Cosette's arrival and revelation**: Learned she was not daughter of old man she called father; another Fauchelevent was real father. **Dowry: five hundred eighty thousand francs, constituted legacy by dead person desiring to remain unknown.** Gillenormand overwhelmed her with gifts: robes, lace, parures, ivory boxes, furnished chamber with elegant trifles.

**Wedding ceremony (1 February 1833, church of Saint-Paul)**: **Cosette wore white taffeta petticoat, Binche guipure robe, English point veil, pearl necklace, orange flower wreath.** Route: Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire. First coach held Cosette, Aunt Gillenormand, M. Gillenormand, Jean Valjean. Marius came in second coach. Exchanged vows, signed registers, exchanged rings, knelt under white moire pall. **During dinner, Basque reported M. Fauchelevent injured hand paining him; begged excuse; would come tomorrow. Jean Valjean rose, gained antechamber unperceived, left during celebration.**

**Jean Valjean's moral crisis**: In Cosette's empty bedroom: no sheets, pillow without case. All Cosette's feminine objects carried away. Only Jean Valjean's bed made up. Questioned: Should he force himself on this happiness? Should he remain sort of father, half seen but respected? Should he present himself as though he had right? Should he bring past to future? Remained twelve long hours of winter night, ice-cold, motionless as corpse. Then shuddered convulsively, kissed Cosette's garments.

## Javert's Death

**Moral transformation**: Javert's certainty crumbled when confronted by Valjean's benevolent nature. All axioms crumbled. Loss of certainty caused supreme anguish.

**Suicide (evening, Place du Châtelet)**: Took off hat, placed on quay edge. Tall black figure appeared erect on parapet, bent towards Seine, drew self up, fell straight down. Dull splash followed. Javert drowned.

## Marius's Crisis of Conscience and Jean Valjean's Decline

**Jean Valjean's revelation (morning after wedding—17 February)**: Very pale, eyes hollow, sunken by sleeplessness. **Proclaimed: "I am an ex-convict."** Justified: conscience implacable; duty places one in hell where God beside you. Entered engagements with himself; keeps them. Revealed situation himself—nothing forced him. If police arrived, exposed through own act, not another's. Chose danger over false name security.

**Marius's shock**: Marius stood with mouth wide open. Pleaded with Jean Valjean not to tell Cosette: "She does not know, it would terrify her. What, a convict!" Jean Valjean seized with convulsion, tears inundating face. Marius later reflected: questioned whether failed in divining Jean Valjean's nature. Admitted chimerical, visionary side. Recalled during six-seven ecstatic weeks in Rue Plumet, never spoke to Cosette of Gorbeau hovel drama or Thénardiers. Accounted for this: benumbed state, intoxication with love, vague dull instinct to conceal. Concluded: even had discovered Jean Valjean convict, would not have changed him or Cosette. Nothing to regret. All was well.

**Jean Valjean's moral grandeur**: Revealed situation himself. Nothing forced him. In avowal there was acceptance of peril. For condemned man, mask is shelter; false name is security. He had rejected false name. Galley-slave might have hidden forever; had withstood temptation through conscientious scruple. Mysterious rehabilitation begun; scruples controlled him. Awakening of conscience is grandeur of soul.

**Marius's doubt about Javert (RUMOR—UNCONFIRMED)**: Recalled Jean Valjean in barricade but did not fight. Had he gone to revenge himself on Javert? Heard behind Rue Mondétour frightful pistol shot. Obvious hatred between police spy and galley-slave. **Jean Valjean had killed Javert. At least, seemed evident.** [RUMOR—Marius has not verified.]

**Marius's metaphysical rationalization**: God visible in affair. Jean Valjean horrible workman but admirable work. Dung-heap aids spring to create rose. Adored Cosette, possessed Cosette, Cosette splendidly pure. What enlightenment needed? Cosette light. Henceforth Marius to fulfill Providence's part to Cosette. Cosette left behind empty chrysalis: Jean Valjean.

**Marius's final conflicted position**: Man was convict—being without place in social ladder. Convict appeared hideous, repulsive. Not examined right man takes to dispose of irrevocable. Not shocked by vengeance. Weakness led to imprudent concession; promised Jean Valjean; must keep word. First duty to Cosette.

**Marius's investigation and moral uncertainty**: Acquired mysterious information about six hundred thousand francs without seeking it. Unable to probe out of respect for promised secret. Believed he had grave duty: restitution of money to someone sought with all possible discretion. In meanwhile, abstained from touching money.

**Chapter 33 domestic arrangements**: Nicolette left. Marius argued cases; Aunt Gillenormand led life peacefully; Jean Valjean came every day.

**Cosette's alienation from Jean Valjean**: Address as _thou_ replaced by _you_, "Madame," "Monsieur Jean," rendering him another person. She became more gay, less tender. Still loved him sincerely. One day chanced to say "father" to him. Flash of joy illuminated Jean Valjean's melancholy countenance. He caught her up: "Say Jean."—"Ah! truly, Monsieur Jean," she replied with laughter. "That is right," said he. Turned aside to wipe eyes. **This was the last time.** Complete extinction ensued. No more familiarity, no more good-morning with kiss. After losing Cosette wholly in one day, afterwards obliged to lose her again in detail.

**Jean Valjean's attempted solace**: When wishing to prolong visits, sang praises of Marius; Cosette outdid him. Never weary. Marius—that word inexhaustible; those six letters contained volumes. In this manner, contrived to remain long time.

**Cosette's confession about dowry**: Chanced to say Marius asked whether she had courage to live on three thousand livres, she answered yes. Marius replied: "I wanted to know."

**Jean Valjean's withdrawal pattern**: During last months of spring and first months of summer 1833, noticed old man neatly clad in black emerged daily at same hour towards nightfall from Rue de l'Homme Armé. Passed Blancs-Manteaux, gained Rue Culture-Sainte-Catherine, reached Rue de l'Écharpe, turned left into Rue Saint-Louis. Soon went only as far as Rue Pavée, shook head, turned back. Then did not overstep Blancs-Manteaux. Pendulum no longer wound up, oscillations growing shorter. Whole countenance expressed single idea: What is use? Eye dim, no radiance. Tears exhausted. Old man's head craned forward; chin moved; folds in gaunt neck painful to behold. Sometimes had umbrella under arm but never opened it.

**Cosette's forgetfulness**: Sometimes Cosette spoke of Jean Valjean, expressed surprise. Marius calmed her: "He is absent, I think. Did not he say he was setting out on a journey?" "That is true," thought Cosette. "He had a habit of disappearing. But not for so long." Two or three times despatched Nicolette to inquire in Rue de l'Homme Armé whether M. Jean had returned. Jean Valjean caused answer "no" to be given.

**Marius's estrangement strategy**: Before marriage, put no questions to M. Fauchelevent; since that time, feared to put any to Jean Valjean. Regretted promise. Confined himself to gradually estranging Jean Valjean from house and effacing him from Cosette's mind. Always placed himself between them. More than effacement, it was eclipse.

**Cosette's magnetism**: Existed between Marius and Cosette all-powerful magnetism causing her to do, instinctively and mechanically, what Marius wished. Conscious of Marius' will in direction of "Monsieur Jean," she conformed to it. Husband had not been obliged to say anything; she yielded to vague but clear pressure of his tacit intentions. Her obedience consisted in not remembering what Marius forgot. Her soul had become so wholly her husband's that which was shrouded in gloom in Marius' mind became overcast in hers. However, concerning Jean Valjean, this forgetfulness was merely superficial. Rather heedless than forgetful. At bottom, sincerely attached to man whom so long called her father; but loved her husband still more dearly. This had somewhat disturbed balance of her heart, which leaned to one side only.

## Jean Valjean's Final Decline (Chapter 33—Late Summer)

**Philosophical digression on natural separation**: That which is called ingratitude of children is not always deserving of reproach. It is ingratitude of nature. Nature divides living beings into those arriving and those departing. Those departing turned towards shadows, those arriving towards light. Hence gulf fatal on part of old, involuntary on part of young. Breach at first insensible increases slowly like separations of branches. Young people feel cooling off of life; old people, that of tomb.

**Physical deterioration**: **A week passed, Jean Valjean had not taken a step in his room. He still remained in bed.** Portress said to husband: "The good man upstairs does not get up, no longer eats, will not last long. That man has his sorrows. His daughter has made a bad marriage." One evening Jean Valjean found difficulty raising himself on elbow; felt wrist, could not find pulse; breath short, halted at times; recognized he was weaker than ever before. Under pressure of supreme preoccupation, made effort, drew himself up into sitting posture, dressed himself in old workingman's clothes. Obliged to pause many times while dressing; putting arms through waistcoat made perspiration trickle from forehead. **One day descended staircase, took three steps in street, seated himself on post where Gavroche had found him meditating on night between 5th and 6th June; remained there few moments, went upstairs again. This was the last oscillation of the pendulum. On following day he did not leave apartment. On day after that, he did not leave bed.**

**Preparations for death**: Took Bishop's candlesticks from chimney-piece, took two wax candles from drawer, put them in candlesticks. Lighted them though broad daylight, summer time. Candles lighted in broad daylight as in chambers where there is corpse. Every step exhausted him; obliged to sit down. Not ordinary fatigue which expends strength to renew it; remnant of all movement possible to him; life drained which flows away drop by drop in overwhelming efforts and never renewed. Chair he allowed himself to fall into placed in front of mirror, so fatal for him, so providential for Marius. He caught sight of himself in mirror, did not recognize himself. **He was eighty years old; before Marius' marriage, would have hardly been taken for fifty; that year had counted for thirty. What he bore on brow was no longer wrinkles of age, but mysterious mark of death. Hollowing of that pitiless nail could be felt there. Cheeks pendulous; skin of face had color leading one to think earth already upon it; corners of mouth drooped as in mask ancients sculptured on tombs. Gazed into space with air of reproach; one would have said he was grand tragic being who had cause to complain of someone.**

**Writing attempt**: As neither pen nor ink had been used for long time, point of pen curled up, ink dried away, he was forced to rise and put few drops of water in ink, which he did not accomplish without pausing and sitting down two or three times. Compelled to write with back of pen. Wiped brow from time to time. Exclaimed within himself [lamentable cries heard by God alone]: "All is over. I shall never see her more. She is a smile which passed over me. I am about to plunge into night without even seeing her again. Oh! one minute, one instant, to hear her voice, to touch her dress, to gaze upon her, the angel! and then to die! What is frightful is to die without seeing her. She would smile on me, she would say a word to me, would that do any harm to any one? No, all is over, and forever. Here I am all alone. My God! My God! I shall never see her again!" At that moment there came a knock at door.

**Thénardier's letter**: Marius took a letter. It smelled of tobacco. Marius recognized that tobacco. Recognized writing as well. Letter superscribed: "To Monsieur, Monsieur le Baron Pommerci. At his hotel." Letter from Thénardier claiming to be in possession of secret concerning individual concerning Marius, offering to drive from family that individual who has no right there, as Madame la Baronne being of lofty birth. Sanctuary of virtue cannot cohabit longer with crime without abdicating.
